title: ACTREC visit (your voice, proud husband)
body:
Some of the bravest people you'll ever meet are under 12.

Recently, my wife [Name] spent an afternoon with children undergoing cancer treatment at ACTREC, Tata Memorial Centre's campus in Kharghar, Navi Mumbai.

The plan was simple: stories, songs, coloured paper and crayons.

Within an hour, the room was full of umbrellas, houses, mountains and birthday cakes, each one held up high with a proud grin. These children spend their weeks moving between chemotherapy, scans and hospital beds. For that one afternoon, they got to just be kids.

A few facts that stayed with us after the visit:

🔹 An estimated 50,000+ children in India are diagnosed with cancer every year.
🔹 In high-income countries, more than 80% of children with cancer are cured. In many low- and middle-income countries, fewer than 30% are. (WHO)
🔹 Most childhood cancers are treatable. What makes the difference is early diagnosis, access to good care, and families being able to complete treatment.

That last point is where India is quietly showing what is possible.

ACTREC is part of Tata Memorial Centre, which works under the Department of Atomic Energy, Government of India. Nearly 4,000 children register for cancer treatment across Tata Memorial's centres every year. ACTREC is also home to India's first public-sector proton therapy centre, and about half of its first 1,000 patients were children.

At Tata Memorial, the share of children who dropped out of cancer treatment fell from about 1 in 4 in 2008 to around 2% in 2022. Medicine alone didn't do that. Free stays near the hospital, nutrition, counselling, financial support and volunteers who keep showing up did.

You don't need to be a doctor to help a child beat cancer:
✅ Know the warning signs: an unexplained lump or swelling, fever that keeps coming back, unusual paleness or bruising, a white glow in the pupil (often noticed in photos), or headaches with early-morning vomiting. If something seems off, see a doctor early.
✅ Donate blood and platelets. Children on chemotherapy need them often.
✅ Give your time, or support organisations that help families stay on treatment.
✅ Share this post. Awareness leads to earlier diagnosis.

[Name], I'm so proud of you. Thank you for reminding me how much a single afternoon can mean to a child.

To the little warriors at ACTREC: keep drawing. Your colours are brighter than anything this disease can throw at you. 💛
notes:
BEFORE YOU POST
[ ] Replace [Name] and tag her LinkedIn profile (type @ and her name) so the post reaches her network too.
[ ] Consent: these photos show children in treatment, so they are identifiable and the context is medical. Confirm with ACTREC or the volunteer group that the photos can be shared publicly and that parents agreed. If unsure, use the shots where the children face away, or blur faces.
[ ] If she went with a group (the orange "V" volunteer lanyards), name and tag that organisation.
[ ] Keep the sources comment below ready to post as the first comment.

SUGGESTED PHOTOS (in this order)
1. Group photo with all the children holding their drawings up. Strongest opening image.
2. Wide shot of the storytelling session, taken from behind the children.
3. The gift moment with the toddler in the orange outfit.
4. The selfie with the girl in the striped top. Only if her parents agreed.

FIRST COMMENT (sources)
Sources for the numbers in this post:
• WHO, Childhood cancer fact sheet: https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/cancer-in-children
• ACTREC, Tata Memorial Centre: https://actrec.gov.in/history
• Proton therapy centre, 1,000 patients: https://www.freepressjournal.in/mumbai/tata-memorials-proton-therapy-centre-hits-1000-cancer-patients-milestone-in-less-than-3-years
• Treatment drop-out at Tata Memorial: https://cancerworld.net/how-indian-centres-slashed-treatment-drop-out-rates-in-childhood-cancer/
• Childhood cancer warning signs: https://www.childhoodcancerinternational.org/facts

title: ACTREC visit (her voice, for her own profile)
body:
I went to ACTREC hoping to brighten a few children's day. They ended up brightening mine.

Recently, I spent an afternoon with children undergoing cancer treatment at ACTREC, Tata Memorial Centre, Kharghar, along with [team / organisation name].

We told stories, sang songs, drew pictures and handed out little art kits. The moment I'll remember: a room full of tiny hands raising their drawings (umbrellas, houses, mountains, a three-tier birthday cake) and waiting for us to cheer. We did. Loudly.

Many of these children spend months away from home and school during treatment. You would never have guessed it from the noise in that room.

What I learned while preparing for this visit:

🔹 An estimated 50,000+ children in India are diagnosed with cancer every year.
🔹 Where good care is accessible, more than 80% of children with cancer are cured. In many low- and middle-income countries, fewer than 30% are. (WHO)
🔹 At Tata Memorial Centre, which works under the Department of Atomic Energy, the share of children dropping out of treatment fell from about 25% in 2008 to around 2% in 2022, helped by free accommodation, nutrition, counselling and financial support.

The doctors here do extraordinary work. ACTREC runs India's first public-sector proton therapy centre, and about half of its first 1,000 patients were children. But a child's recovery also depends on whether the family can stay, eat, cope and keep coming back. That part needs all of us.

If you'd like to help:
✅ Learn the early warning signs of childhood cancer and share them with parents you know.
✅ Donate blood and platelets.
✅ Volunteer, or support organisations that help families complete treatment.

Thank you to the ACTREC team and fellow volunteers for the work they do every single day, and to the children for showing me what courage really looks like. 💛
